title: mini-latency-variance-lab
content:
Purpose: quick, repeatable probe to surface p99 variance when switching between small micro-batches and single-request multiplexing. Notes to self: try to keep experiment surface minimal (1 model, 1 GPU class) so noise is easier to attribute.

Environment:
- Model: llama-2-13b-quant (prod-like quant profile)
- Hardware: g5.12x (48GB), single GPU pinned
- Runtime: serve-v1.9.1-local with my debug flags
- Dataset: 2000 synthetic prompts (avg token length 120, 10% long tails ~600 tokens)
- KV cache: Cold vs warm runs included

Commands (local harness):
- cold: python run_harness.py --model llama-2-13b-quant --gpu g5.12x --concurrency 1 --batch-size 1 --warmup 0 --requests 2000 --save results/cold.txt
- micro-batch: --batch-size 4 --concurrency 8 --mux false
- mux: --batch-size 1 --concurrency 32 --mux true --mux-window-ms 5

Quick raw table (p50/p95/p99 in ms, qps):
- Cold single (b=1,c=1): p50=95, p95=320, p99=610, qps=10
- Warm single (b=1,c=1): p50=48, p95=160, p99=260, qps=18
- Micro b4,c8 (prefetch cache warm): p50=42, p95=120, p99=310, qps=120
- Mux b1,c32 (warm): p50=39, p95=150, p99=420, qps=250
- Mux w/short-window (3ms) p99 rises -> 470ms (more preemption), qps ~270
- Micro w/kv-thrashing (mixed tenants) p99 -> 520ms, qps drops to 85

Observations / quick hypotheses:
1) Micro-batching stabilizes p95 well but can create long p99 tails when a single request lands at tail of a batch that experiences slow IO (observed when disk-backed tokenizer cache miss occurred).
2) Multiplexing (mux) gives best raw qps but suffers higher p99 under contention; widening the mux window reduced p99 slightly at cost of avg latency.
3) Cold cache penalty huge (p99 >600ms). Need prewarm on model load for burst scenarios.
4) KV-cache thrashing (multi-tenant simulation) destroys both qps and p99; eviction churn visible in logs at ~t=30s.

Diagnostic notes (logs/traces to inspect):
- trace ids: sample traces saved in results/traces/trace_{runid}.json (check scheduling_events and io_wait_ms)
- kernel metrics: sm_efficiency dips correlated with p99 spikes in micro-batch runs

Actionable next steps (short):
- Re-run warm micro-batch with tokenizer cache pinned to ramfs to confirm IO hypothesis (run id: micro-ramfs-2025-02-04).
- Try mux-window sweep: 1ms, 3ms, 10ms to find elbow for p99 vs qps tradeoff.
- Add synthetic tenant noise to micro-batch runs to quantify eviction threshold.
- Open small PR to add an opt-in "batch-head-priority" which preempts long-tail items out of batches after X ms (prototype in PR #842).

Open questions / unknowns:
- How representative is synthetic token-length mix vs real traffic (ask product for sample traces).
- Does warmup scheme need to be per-tenant or global? memory footprint implications.
- Can we get kernel-level telemetry in prod without 3x overhead? (talk to infra team, ENG-4127).

Notes to self:
- Keep all runs reproducible: record random seed, harness commit SHA, and GPU frequency governor state.
- When filing follow-up ticket, attach minimal reproducer from harness and one trace where p99>400ms.

Attachments / where to find outputs:
- results/ (CSV per-run), results/traces/, results/plots/ (quick matplotlib PNGs)
- local harness commit: serve-harness @ a1b2c3d

If I forget: immediate takeaways = prewarm + small mux-window (5-8ms) seems promising for our workload, but batch-head-priority may be required to cap p99 under noisy tenants.

Slack ping draft to SRE/product: 
"hey @sre / @product — ran quick mini-lab on micro-batch vs mux for llama-2-13b-quant. Micro gives stable p95 but mux gives higher qps and worse p99 under tenant noise. Will create a small PR for batch-head-priority and propose a warmup hook for Dedicated. Posting raw csv and a couple traces in #runtime-bench. TL;DR: prewarm + mux-window tuning buys most wins, but eviction churn remains painful."
